icd10_codes.description: Exposure to excessive natural heat, initial encounter
Farm field as the place of occurrence of the external cause
Civilian activity done for income or pay

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , {PATIENT_FIRST} . i'm doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . how are you feeling now that you've had some fluids ?
[patient] better . a lot better than when i came in . i still feel kind of weak .
[doctor] okay . that's expected . can you tell me what happened today ?
[patient] so i work for {ORG} , picking strawberries . we start at six in the morning . today it was really hot , they said it was going to be ninety eight , and there's no shade out in the field at all , it's just rows and rows .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] i was bent over picking all morning , and around one o'clock i started getting a really bad headache and i felt dizzy . i was sweating like crazy , my shirt was soaked . and then i felt like i was going to throw up . and my legs started cramping .
[doctor] okay . did you pass out ?
[patient] no , i did n't pass out . i felt like i was going to , everything kind of went gray , so i sat down in the dirt between the rows . my crew leader {OTHER_FIRST} saw me and brought me over to the truck and put the air conditioning on and gave me water . and then they called the ambulance because i threw up the water .
[doctor] okay . how much water were you drinking during the morning ?
[patient] not enough . i had one bottle . the water cooler is at the end of the rows and we get paid by the box , so you do n't want to stop .
[doctor] i understand . did you take any breaks ?
[patient] one break , at like nine thirty .
[doctor] okay . were you confused at all ? did anybody say you were acting strange or not making sense ?
[patient] no , i knew where i was the whole time . i was just really tired and sick .
[doctor] okay , that's important . any chest pain or trouble breathing ?
[patient] my heart was pounding , but no chest pain .
[doctor] okay . any medical problems ?
[patient] no . i'm usually really healthy . i came up from california for the season with my two sisters , and this is my third year doing this .
[doctor] do you take any medicines ? water pills , anything for allergies ?
[patient] no , nothing .
[doctor] any alcohol or drugs ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and have you had this happen before ?
[patient] last summer i got a little dizzy once , but i just sat in the shade and it went away .
[doctor] okay . so when you came in , the paramedics measured your temperature at one hundred and one point two , your heart rate was one twenty two , and your blood pressure was ninety eight over sixty . you were sweaty and flushed , but you were awake and talking normally .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we gave you two liters of iv fluid , and some ondansetron for the nausea , and cooled you down with ice packs and the fan . now your temperature is ninety nine point one , your heart rate is eighty eight , and your blood pressure is one twelve over seventy . on exam , your skin is still a little warm , your mouth is a little dry , and your neurological exam is completely normal , you're alert and oriented , no confusion , strength is normal .
[patient] that's good .
[doctor] it is . so we checked some labs . your sodium was a little low at one thirty three , your kidney function is normal , and your muscle enzyme , the ck , was normal , so there's no sign of muscle breakdown . your urine was concentrated , which tells me you were very dehydrated .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so what you had is heat exhaustion . it's from working hard for a long time out in the heat and the sun without enough water and rest . the important part is that you did n't have any confusion and your temperature never got really high , so this was not heat stroke , which is much more dangerous .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] but heat exhaustion can turn into heat stroke if you keep pushing , so we need to take it seriously .
[patient] okay . can i go back to work tomorrow ?
[doctor] i'd like you to take tomorrow off and rest , drink plenty of fluids , and you can use an electrolyte drink . then when you go back , you need to take a break in the shade every hour , and drink a cup of water every fifteen to twenty minutes , even if you're not thirsty . i'm going to write a note for your employer saying that , and that you need access to water and shade .
[patient] thank you . that will help .
[doctor] wear a wide brim hat and light loose clothes , and try to do the hardest work early in the morning . if you start getting a headache , dizziness , cramps , or nausea again , stop , go to the shade , and drink water . and if you get confused , stop sweating , or faint , that's an emergency , call nine one one .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we'll keep you here for another hour to finish the fluids and make sure you can drink without throwing up . then you can go home . if you need anything , our clinic number is {PHONE} .
[patient] okay , thank you so much .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Heat-related illness.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old female with no significant past medical history who presents by ambulance from her workplace on {DATE_NUM} with heat-related illness.

The patient is employed by {ORG} as a strawberry harvester. She began work at 6:00 AM in an open farm field without shade, with ambient temperature reportedly 98 degrees Fahrenheit. She had one bottle of water and one break during the morning. At approximately 1:00 PM, she developed severe headache, dizziness, profuse sweating, nausea, and leg cramps, followed by near-syncope. She did not lose consciousness. She was placed in an air-conditioned vehicle and given water, which she vomited. She reports palpitations but denies chest pain or dyspnea. She denies confusion; she was oriented throughout. No medications, diuretics, alcohol, or drug use. Prior mild heat-related dizziness last summer.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Vital Signs: On EMS arrival, temperature 101.2 F, heart rate 122, blood pressure 98/60. After treatment, temperature 99.1 F, heart rate 88, blood pressure 112/70.
Skin: Warm, mildly flushed. Dry mucous membranes.
Neurological: Alert and oriented x3. No confusion. Strength normal throughout.

RESULTS

Sodium 133 (mildly low). Creatinine within normal limits. Creatine kinase within normal limits. Urinalysis: concentrated urine, elevated specific gravity.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Heat exhaustion.
• Medical Reasoning: Prolonged strenuous agricultural work in a farm field in excessive natural heat with inadequate hydration and rest. Core temperature below 104 F and normal mental status; no evidence of heat stroke. No rhabdomyolysis. Mild hyponatremia consistent with volume depletion.
• Medical Treatment: Normal saline 2 L IV, ondansetron 4 mg IV, active cooling with ice packs and fan. Observe for tolerance of oral intake prior to discharge.
• Patient Education and Counseling: Oral hydration with electrolyte solution. Warning signs of heat stroke reviewed.

2. Occupational exposure to extreme heat.
• Work: Off work for 1 day. On return, hourly rest breaks in the shade, water every 15 to 20 minutes, access to water and shade; work note provided to employer.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.
